basis: The Commission reports in 2026 that new legislation opened certain technical, specialised and auxiliary public administration posts to EU citizens, answering its repeated finding that EU citizens had no access to such posts.

The Government states that Government Decision No. 566/2025 lets persons without Moldovan citizenship fill technical, specialist and auxiliary posts, which addresses the closure of public sector posts.
The Commission states that the law establishes the legal basis for implementing EU social security coordination rules.
The Government's note states that the draft creates the framework to apply Articles 64 and 65 of Regulation (EC) No 883/2004 on unemployment benefits.
The Government's accession programme lists the draft decision as guaranteeing the rights of unemployed EU citizens, which concerns the application of coordination to unemployment.
The Commission states that the law establishes the legal basis for EESSI interconnection.
The Government plans and prepares the digital infrastructure to join EESSI, which the 2025 and 2026 key recommendations ask for.
The Commission reports the designation of the e-Governance Agency as EESSI National Access Point in February 2026, after the 2025 recommendation on EESSI.
The Commission reports the designation of the two bodies as EESSI liaison bodies in February 2026.
The Government's accession programme lists interconnecting Moldova's social security system with those of Member States, which is the subject of the issue.
The Government's accession programme lists technical documentation for interoperability between the health insurance system and EESSI.
The Government states that interoperability between the employment agency and EESSI will be provided in the new agency information system.
The Government states that Romanian courses will be offered to EU and EEA citizens, their family members and children enrolled in Moldovan schools.
The 2023 key recommendation asked Moldova to adopt the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, and it was adopted in September 2023.
The 2023 report asked for a governance body for the strategy, and the 2024 report records the National Council for Digital Transformation set up in November 2023 to coordinate it.
The Commission records in 2025 the implementation programme for 2025 to 2027 as a step in implementing the strategy.
The strategy and the Government's implementation report propose a Strategic Delivery Unit in the e-Governance Agency to strengthen implementation capacity, which the key recommendation asks for.
The Reform Agenda commits to making more tax services available electronically, which is the subject of the issue and of the 2026 report's call for further digitalisation.
The e-invoice service on the Electronic Fiscal Services platform is an electronic service for taxpayers.
The Government states that the programme was approved in line with the Commission's recommendation, and the 2026 report records its adoption under e-Health.
The Reform Agenda sets electronic health records for 40% of the insured population by December 2027, addressing the lack of an integrated, interoperable system found in 2024.
The Reform Agenda commits to a legal framework for digital health services aligned with EU recommendations, after finding no approved eHealth regulatory framework.
The Government plans a national e-Health entity, addressing the lack of a dedicated institutional framework it identifies.
The ePrescription system was approved in January 2024 and operated from April 2024, after the 2023 report found limited progress on e-health, and the Commission reports it under e-health.
The Government states that Law No. 72/2025 transposes the European Electronic Communications Code, as the 2023 to 2025 recommendations asked.
The Government states that Law No. 81/2025 transposes Regulation (EU) 2022/612 on roaming, as the 2023 to 2025 key recommendations asked.
The Reform Agenda and the Commission's 2026 assessment present the secondary legislation as implementing the Electronic Communications Code and the Roaming Regulation.
The Commission reports amended secondary legislation aligning with the remaining EU roaming acquis, as the 2025 key recommendation asked.
The Commission states that Law No. 106/2026 transposes the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, which the 2025 report asked Moldova to implement.
The Government states that the Association Council decision moved roaming market opening to a new stage and amended the annex on electronic communications.
The regulator states that it drafted and adopted the regulatory acts needed to implement Law No. 72/2025 and Law No. 81/2025.
The Reform Agenda commits to a broadband mapping system after finding that its absence restricts monitoring, investment and the targeting of subsidies.
The Government plans a geographical survey of broadband coverage under Law No. 72/2025 to support the targeting of investment.
The Government plans to develop networks in identified white areas, which addresses broadband investment for underserved areas.
The Government's accession programme lists a draft Competition Council regulation on state aid for broadband networks, which the issue names.
The Commission notes in 2025 that legislative work to align with the Digital Services Act has started, and the Government lists the draft law on digital services.
The Government proposes the regulator as Digital Services Coordinator, and the Commission reports initial steps on the institutional framework for the Digital Services Act in 2026.
The Government states that the Competition Council is designated for Law No. 53/2025 and is to be designated for the Digital Markets Act.
The Government states that Law No. 53/2025 partly transposes the platform-to-business regulation, on which the Commission found no alignment from 2023 to 2025.
The Government states that the 2025 geo-blocking law partly transposes Regulation (EU) 2018/302, on which the Commission found no alignment from 2023 to 2025.
The Government plans to amend Competition Law No. 183/2012 to provide national implementation mechanisms for the Digital Markets Act.
The Government lists a draft amendment to Law No. 53/2025, after noting that the platform-to-business regulation is not fully transposed as regards enforcement measures.
The Commission states that implementation of the Digital Moldova 2020 strategy was only partially successful, with 6 of its 12 targets achieved.

The Court of Accounts states that, as a result of the e-Governance Agency coordinating ICT procurement under the methodology, conditions were created to secure the State's rights over systems delivered.
The Commission states that the voluntary roaming arrangements between EU and Moldovan operators provide tangible benefits to the public and businesses.
The source reports that since the start of 2024 all mobile operators offer significantly reduced roaming tariffs in 30 EU and EEA countries, following the 2023 agreement it describes.
The source reports the regulators' finding that the average roaming basket fell by almost 70% for Moldovan users under the Moldova-Romania agreement.
The Commission states that extending Roam Like at Home to Moldova from January 2026 removed roaming charges and brought immediate benefits.
The Government states that Law No. 81/2025, the Association Council decision and secondary acts created all the legislative preconditions to join Roam Like at Home.
The Commission states that the alignment achieved, including Law No. 72/2025, facilitates the roll-out of higher speed and affordable networks and services.
The regulator states that the frequency licence competitions ensured additional use of spectrum and contributed to network capacity and 5G roll-out.
